name: Snagging, defects and handover lists
one_line: The numbered list of things that are wrong, each pinned to a location and a responsible trade, tracked through re-inspections until it is closed — the pre-completion snagging list, the client's or buyer's own list, the handover and practical-completion schedule, and the defects raised during the liability period after the works are finished and everybody has left. Its defining property is that it is a TRACKER with a lifecycle: the same document is re-issued repeatedly with a status column changing, and it is the last live thing on a project everyone else considers closed. The row stands on ONE leg of the node test — detection signals — and its dimensions and privacy posture are the schema's, which is recorded here rather than hidden. Absorbs the legacy row cons.snagging. Placeholder row (J-IND, written to J-DEPTH): it writes NO field rows, because the construction_property schema declares none.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry below is a DETECTION signal and never an extraction licence. The construction_property schema declares no field rows (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6), so nothing here writes a domain fact; detection exists so the material is recognised, kept where this row’s sensitivity says, and offered honestly. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

the defect-register structure, which is this row's fingerprint: a table whose columns read item number, location (plot, room, level or grid reference), a description of what is wrong, a responsible trade or subcontractor, a raised date, a target or due date, a status, and a closed or verified date, with one row per fault. The pairing of a LOCATION column with a STATUS column is what no other table in this family has. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”

a re-issue sequence: the same register exported repeatedly with a rising count of closed rows and a falling count of open ones, so the corpus contains near-duplicate spreadsheets or PDFs distinguished only by a date and a status column. This row generates more version families than any other in the construction schema.
a photograph pack keyed to item numbers: images whose filenames or an accompanying schedule carry the register's item numbers, frequently with an annotation, arrow or circle drawn onto the image.
a snagging-app export: a per-item PDF card carrying a thumbnail, a location, a description, an assignee and a status, repeated identically for every item — a layout no human produces by hand.

a handover or practical-completion document set: a certificate or statement of practical completion accompanied by an outstanding-works schedule and a defects-liability period stated with a start and an end date.
a defect notification during the liability period: a dated letter or email from a client or buyer describing a fault, referencing a completion date, and requiring attendance within a stated period.
a close-out or de-snag confirmation: the same register with every status closed, signed off by an inspecting party, sometimes with a making-good certificate.
parent-folder context naming a plot, a unit, a handover or a defects period, treated as a clue once one of the structures above is present. Folder context never fires alone.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: defect registers name individual tradespeople as responsible parties and, in residential work, name the occupant whose home is faulty. Any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

the central determination for this row: separating a DEFECT (something built wrong, to be put right under an existing obligation) from a VARIATION (something the client now wants differently, to be paid for). The two are argued about precisely because the same item is presented as each by the two sides, and the register row often reads identically.
separating a contractor's own snagging list from the CLIENT's list of the same building. Same items, same rooms, opposite authorship, and the canonical field list has no key for the role.
an unlabelled defect note: a photograph with a scrawled arrow, or a three-line email saying the kitchen door binds, with no item number and no register around it.
separating a defects register from a maintenance or repairs log. Both are located, statused fault lists; only one sits under a completion obligation with an end date.

a purpose-coherent handover file whose members are individually unremarkable — a completion certificate, a register, a photograph set, an operating manual and a warranty. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
in every case above, abstention is the required outcome where the evidence does not settle it. “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”
never_alone: an item-numbered table alone. Numbered rows with statuses are also an action log, a risk register, a bug tracker export, an audit finding list, a punch list in manufacturing and a to-do list.
the word 'snag', 'defect', 'punch list' or 'outstanding works' in a filename. Software teams, manufacturers and event producers all use at least two of them.

a UK-style postcode or a street address alone. An address is the single most tempting token in this whole family and it appears in every role at once — the site, the client’s home, the contractor’s registered office, the architect’s letterhead, a supplier’s depot, and a comparable property cited in a report. 00 states the same ambiguity for a university name: “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” — the address case is worse, and this is recorded as inference because 00 writes that sentence about a university, not an address.

an annotated photograph alone. A circled crack is a defect photo, a survey photo, an inventory photo, an insurance claim photo and a progress photo, and nothing in the image says which. “conflicting signals should lead to abstention rather than an invented classification”
a trade name alone (electrician, plasterer). It appears as a responsible party, an author, a supplier, an addressee and a heading.
a status word alone — open, closed, outstanding, complete. It is the most generic vocabulary in the entire catalogue.

source_type or extension alone. “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”, and file_kind_plausible is constitutionally never-alone (CONNECTION section 5, invariant 2).
membership in a download session — a whole project folder or a document-portal export pulled down at once. “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”
a bare 4-digit number read as a year. It is at least as often a drawing number, a job number, a plot number, a house number, a cost code, or a British Standard reference.

a PDF author, producer, or company metadata string alone. “PDF metadata should be treated as supporting evidence, not as truth” — one contractor’s template stamps the same firm on every blank form it ever generated.

a defect photograph's membership in a site walk. construction_property.progress-photos is recognised by capture metadata, rhythm and place, and this row is not — this row is recognised by the register's document structure. A photograph enters this row through an item number or through membership in an accepted register, NEVER through capture metadata, a GPS cluster or a work-hours rhythm. That sibling's line is adopted unchanged here: ‘a measure, a marker or a caption identifying a fault, or membership in an accepted defect list’ is what supports this row.

a location or room column alone. Room-by-room tables are also inventories, schedules of condition, asset registers, measured surveys, fire-door registers and room data sheets; the column pairs with a STATUS and a RESPONSIBLE TRADE or it is evidence of nothing here.

a defects-liability or rectification period stated in a document. It is a CONTRACT TERM and it is printed in the contract particulars, the subcontract order, the payment schedule and the collateral warranty long before any defect exists. Only a period that is RUNNING, evidenced by dated activity after a completion date, is this row's signal.

work_types: warranty or latent-defect claim under a completed contract
grouping_reasons: one plot, unit or property and every defect ever raised on it — the clearest group in this row and the one that persists after the project itself is closed.
one register across its re-issues, joined by the universal duplicate_family and version_family facts rather than by any construction fact. This is the row where those universals do the most work.

one defect: the notification, the photographs, the trade's response, the re-inspection and the sign-off — purpose-coherent even where the members share no content. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
one handover event: the certificate, the outstanding-works schedule, the manuals and the warranties.
no group at all is a valid outcome: a single annotated photograph with no register around it is an ordinary standalone image.
and the stop rules apply as written — “when members carry irreconcilable course, institution, project, term, or purpose facts” — two plots' registers in one folder do not merge.

and a distinction this row must keep, borrowed from the deepened project row: a defect item is a POSITION INSIDE A JOB in the browse sense, and being browsed under a job is not evidence about the file. Item 44 sits under the plot in the tree; what activates is the register.

template.why: Empty by binding contract: a dimension may only branch on a field the same entry’s schema declares, and construction_property declares none (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, CONNECTION PR-6). That is a contract fact, not a claim that this situation has no shape — it plainly does, and it is recorded here as PROSE for whoever answers the schema row’s open_question. The recommendation, held as prose: the site or project first, then the plot or unit where there is more than one, then the defect phase (pre-completion snagging / handover outstanding works / defects-period faults), with the register itself and its photographs kept together under the item. An item number is meaningless without its plot — item 44 exists on every plot on a development — which is 00's own reason for putting a course above a homework number. The phase level matters more here than it looks: the same list before completion and after it carries different obligations and different money. 00’s own ordering reason applies: “a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child”. Not time-first — “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” Time is a poor level here because a single defect's life crosses months and a register's re-issues are versions, not periods. And whatever eventually lands stays a recommendation: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: The load-bearing collision on this row, and the one that decides who pays. The same physical item is a DEFECT (built wrong, put right free under an existing obligation) or a VARIATION (wanted differently, paid for) depending entirely on which side's paper you read. The discriminating evidence: a status column, a responsible trade and a re-inspection history support this row; a numbered instruction reference, a quantified cost and time consequence, and an approval or notice support the variation row. Where a document carries both, it is genuinely both and the disagreement is the point. Provenance: inference.

Recorded deliberately, because the node test asked whether this row is only a work_type of the project. The discriminating evidence: a defects-liability period, a re-issue sequence with a status column, and activity AFTER practical completion support this row; anything inside the construction period supports the project row. The registers of a project that has closed are the clearest case that this is a separate situation. SETTLED, and not by this row alone: the project row has since been deepened, has DEMOTED the defects half of its completion triple out of its own activation evidence, and states the concession in its own words — ‘the sibling recorded this collision deliberately because its own node test asked whether it is merely a work_type of this row; it is not, and this row concedes the point.’ The practical-completion certificate itself stays with the project row as the boundary event; this row claims the outstanding-works schedule appended to it, and the shared fixture is named on both sides. Provenance: inference.

A check-out report and a snagging list are both located, photographed, costed fault lists. The discriminating evidence: a tenancy, a tenant, a deposit reference and a check-in comparison support the inventory row; a completion date, a trade responsibility column and a defects period support this row. Provenance: inference.

A non-conformance register is the same table with the same columns in a factory, and both trace a fault to a responsible party and a closure. The discriminating evidence: a part or batch number, a specification clause and a corrective-action methodology support the manufacturing row; a room, a plot and a trade support this row. Provenance: inference.

Issue logs, action registers and punch lists in general project management have this row's exact structure, and software issue exports are the tempting false file. The discriminating evidence: a physical location and a trade support this row; a component, an assignee and a sprint or milestone support the delivery row. Provenance: inference.

An independent snagging inspection is sold, priced and addressed like a professional report. The discriminating evidence: an item-numbered, located, statused list intended to be worked through supports this row; condition ratings, a basis of valuation and a reliance clause support the valuation row. Provenance: inference.

A latent-defect or warranty claim after completion is simultaneously this row's defect and that row's claim, especially for installed products. The discriminating evidence: a product serial number, a manufacturer and a warranty policy support the warranty row; a plot, a trade and a contractual defects period support this row. Provenance: inference.

Retention is released against defects being closed, so the register and the account cite each other. The discriminating evidence: a valuation number, a retention percentage and a certified sum support the final-account row; an item list with statuses supports this row. Provenance: inference.

RECIPROCAL, and the sibling stated its side first; its wording is adopted rather than re-authored. ‘A defect close-up and a progress frame are adjacent captures from one walk. The discriminating evidence: a measure, a marker or a caption identifying a fault, or membership in an accepted defect list, supports the snagging row; a record of the state of the works supports this row.’ The deeper point, which this row must not blur: that sibling earned its node on a DIFFERENT DETECTION METHOD — capture metadata, rhythm and place — and this row makes no such claim. This row is recognised by document structure like every other row on the schema; its photographs are grouped MEMBERS of a register, never its activation evidence. Provenance: inference.

ADDED THIS PASS, reversing the gist pass's judgement that no edge was owed. The gist memo said the two rows share no evidence item; that was wrong. A buyer's own snagging list of the new house they have just bought, and the builder's list of the same house, are frequently THE SAME BYTES — the buyer is sent the register. The landed row claims a householder's own record of their own home and lists inspection, warranty and completion certificates among its own work_types. The discriminating evidence is the schema anchor's seam and this row does not re-draw it: an INSTRUCTION — a job or contract reference, a responsible-trade column, a defects period running under a contract, a re-inspection history — supports this row; an owner's own file about their own home with no instruction around it supports the landed row. An address selects neither. Shared fixture: 'Snag list - our new house.xlsx'. R1c owes the reciprocal; the landed row does not name construction_property. Provenance: inference.

ADDED THIS PASS. A block manager's repairs and works log is a located, statused, trade-assigned fault list on a building, and it never ends. The discriminating evidence: a CLOSING obligation — a completion date, a defects period with an end, a retention release, a making-good certificate — supports this row; a standing management appointment, leaseholder reporting, apportionment and a service-charge year support the block row. A perpetual log is not a defects register with the word 'perpetual' in front of it; it is a different situation. Provenance: inference.

ADDED THIS PASS, because the row's own needs_llm names the defects-versus-maintenance separation and the gist pass left it without an edge. A maintenance work order and a defect item both name a fault, a location, an assignee and a closure. The discriminating evidence: an asset or equipment identifier, a planned-maintenance schedule, a meter reading and a fault CODE support the maintenance row; a plot or room, a responsible TRADE, and a contractual defects period with an end date support this row. The deciding question is whether the work is done under a warranty of workmanship that expires, or under an upkeep regime that does not. Provenance: inference.

also_holds_with.signal: A defect notification served under a contract, a latent-defect claim and a pre-action letter about defective work are legal records as well as this situation's, and legal is a safety domain: “Finance, identity, medical, and legal material should be implemented first as safety domains”. Co-activation is correct and protective ordering applies — the legal reading protects first and this row's reading is additive. “One file may hold facts from more than one domain without losing information.”

An annotated defect photograph carries the photos schema's capture facts as well as being a register member. The sibling construction_property.progress-photos already states the capture side and this row does not reopen it; what is recorded here is only that both readings hold of the same bytes. “One file may hold facts from more than one domain without losing information.”

Retention is released against defects being closed, so a close-out confirmation is simultaneously a finance record for whoever's books the release lands in and this situation's evidence that the list is finished. Neither reading displaces the other; the collision with construction_property.final-account is a separate and narrower matter and is recorded there.

falls_through_to.why: The commonest honest outcome in this row: a register export, an app archive or a fault email whose plot and phase are unresolved. Registers are famously untitled. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The home for a standalone completion certificate, making-good certificate or outstanding-works schedule with no project file around it. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The home for a single annotated defect photograph with no register around it — a very large population in this row. “One-Off Images may live under Photos/One-Off Images and hold images with no event, project, reference collection, or photo-family association.”

Screenshots of snagging-app screens are among this row's most numerous and least valuable members. “Temporary Screenshots may live under Photos/Temporary Screenshots and hold screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship.”

Residential defect files name an occupant and the faults in the home they live in, and independent inspection reports name an addressee; the row's people-bearing members belong here. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

Password-protected snagging-platform exports and proprietary app bundles are ordinary here. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

sensitivity_why: Two reasons, both about people rather than about buildings. A residential defect file names an occupant and catalogues everything wrong with the home they live in, which is information about a private individual's living conditions; and a defect register names individual tradespeople as responsible for failures, which is material that can affect their work. 00's corpus sentence covers the category the moment either appears: the corpus “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records”. Most of this row is dull item lists and the value is set for the members that are not. This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; the handling class is P7's and is not set here.
open_question: Two, and the first is new to this pass. (1) The row stands on ONE leg of CONNECTION.md §2's test. Its detection signals differ from the schema's default — the defect register is a fifth structure alongside the family's title block, measured-works table, previously-certified valuation arithmetic and apportionment schedule — and that is sufficient, since any one leg suffices. But its recommended dimensions are the family default with a plot sub-level added, and its privacy posture is the schema's own; NEITHER distinguishes it, and both are recorded here as failing rather than claimed. Whether one leg is enough for a row this narrow is R1c's, and it is the same question the deepened project row asks about itself. (2) Whether the DEFECT/VARIATION boundary is decidable by the product at all. The honest answer recorded here is that it often is not, because the two sides disagree on purpose and both readings are written down in good faith — so the correct behaviour is to recognise both and abstain rather than to pick, which is 00's own instruction for conflicting signals: “conflicting signals should lead to abstention rather than an invented classification”. What is Joseph's, and is not resolved here, is whether a file that is genuinely both should be offered in two places or held in one.
